- 23.04.2017 | Food and Agriculture
- By Dr. Eva Krüger
Food is a good starting point for thinking about climate change. But what’s really driving climate change in the first place?
In the past few years, there has been much debate on how to tackle global warming. Some say we can simply reduce our carbon footprint by reducing our energy use and other things. Others argue that it is time to focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuels – a major problem for climate change.
But which side are you on?
A recent study has found that the amount of heat trapped in the Earth’s atmosphere has increased by around 13% per degree Celsius (1.4 degrees Fahrenheit). This means that warming the planet by 10C would increase global temperatures by a mean of about 2.8°F, and this is already happening.
The report was released on December 8th by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) at its annual meeting in Geneva, Switzerland. It looks at data from different parts of the world to determine how much heat the Earth’s atmosphere has trapped over the past century. This can help scientists to understand how much warming will happen in the future.
